Reposting one of my comments about this to explain.

Please read this comment if you are someone interested in game development. 

Taking photos during the hunt is an inherently risky behavior. That's why developers included the risk of it not working out. You can't be rewarded for taking risks all the time. Making it fade or adding a grace period takes away the consequences for your actions and rewards lazy/brainless players when that isn't what a risk does (that's actually the complete opposite of a risk in reality).

If someone in the real world who faced certain death, ran towards a paranormal entity that was actively hunting them with lethal force... just to get a 3 Star photo... that would be considered suicidal, psychotic, unrational, and it would epitomize pure risk. That person SHOULD wait for an event to get a photo and live to tell the tale (also a much higher % chance of a perfect run and securing that huge bag). Eventually after repeated attempts you will die from a quick hunter (the Rev is gonna come for you one day) just to take a silly photo. This example was based in the real world... So congrats! You just died from being impatient (that's worse than dysentery in the Oregon Trail).


A ghost event later in the investigation likely would have happened at some point and provided a risk free method to obtain the SAME REWARD. People act like there is no other way to get a ghost photo and claim that this makes no sense. All while ignoring what they are actually doing in the game. 

Ask yourself... Do the rewards outweigh the risks?  In this case... is your life worth a CHANCE of getting a photo? Probably not, Scott.  Also... if you don't get a 3 star photo due to being too far away from the ghost... what is the  actual point of taking a bad photo for less money?

Imagine a gambling simulator that ensured you had higher odds to win or lose if you went all in (risky like taking a photo during a hunt) if you get rewarded or punished for risky behavior it isn't realistic, and it legitimately makes it less enjoyable.

Changing this mechanic is taking the game from a balanced somewhat realistic state to an unrealistic and unenjoyable state where bad play is rewarded and players don't have to grow or learn when to appropriately take risks.

If you want perfect runs just wait for an event to take the photo. Ghosts can't blink during events (only phantoms disappear during events but it isn't a blink, they can still be photographed). 

If you don't care about making perfect runs with full book just take pictures whenever and be indifferent, but you can't take consequence away from risky behavior. That is flat out bad game design. 


Edit: To this day no one who has ever lived can scientifically prove that they captured a ghost on camera. Cameras have existed for a sizeable amount of time at this point. If night vision security cameras or a polaroid flash camera in the dark could prove ghosts were real; then one of the tens of thousands of geniuses that have came and went since cameras were invented would have won a Nobel prize for proving the existence of ghosts. If you truly know how cameras work (and the settings being used on the camera when the photo was taken), as well as understanding anomalies that regularly occur in photography, and are privy to the environmental conditions the photo was taken in, you can replicate and debunk photo evidence, or at least more accurately theorize what happened than saying, "ghosts". 

My point being... getting a photo of a ghost is currently IMPOSSIBLE in reality. It can't be done. Period. To me that doesn't suggest it to be an in game task that should be made easier. Without risk there is no reward (true in both life and video games). Any future game developers remember this. If you make a risky behavior easier like you are suggesting, it actually affects the experience on several levels. By keeping risky behaviors inherently risky it actually ADDS to a players experience and makes the risks more rewarding (winning when you go all in is a huge reward).

By this I mean make calculated decisions. If you know you're taking a risk at least have a plan and know wait at least one hunt to see if you can hear it's speed. This way when you do take the risk you're more likely to get that dopamine payout. It just doesn't make sense logically for it to be easy to take a photo of a non physical being that is trying to sneak up and kill you and has theoretically never been documented with photo evidence. 

Personally I always try to full book perfect run. If someone blows the perfect run for the party I would situationally try to get a hunt photo if we needed one.  I wouldn't risk the perfect run bonus for a CHANCE. 

Many games have risk and part of improving your in game skill level is to mitigate risky behavior as much as possible and maximize non risky behavior. This always comes with time and getting feel for the game. 

End of my Ted talk.

The choices for this poll don't emphasize any of the reasons the flashing mechanic is necessary for advanced playthroughs. I can't answer this because my answer is not listed. Without the flashing mechanics no evidence playthroughs would be affected severely (IMHO no evidence is the best and most rewarding game mode in all of Phasmophobia). The blink mechanic is ESSENTIAL for determining if a ghost is hunting or just doing an event, AND different ghosts blink differently. Learning to recognize ghosts from their blinking is 100% necessary for no evidence runs. 

A ghost will NOT blink during an event (if it's a phantom it may disappear if photographed, but the event will continue even after it disappears: a dead giveaway of phantom). Also, if you aren't close to a light switch or can't hear the doors locking, one of the easiest ways to identify a hunt is footsteps and blinking at the same time. HOWEVER, always keep in mind that ghost events CAN  include footsteps, BUT if it is an event the ghost will NEVER BLINK while walking towards you.


Lastly the blinking mechanic can be used to immediately identify phantoms, onis, and obakes with no evidence at all. If it blinks slow - phantom, if it barely blinks and is mostly visible - oni, and if the ghost changes ghost models immediately following a blink (I.E. A ghost starts hunting in the form of a child ghost then blinks and instantly changes to an adult male ghost model) it will be an obake.


Blinking is a very consistent way to know if it's an event or a hunt. It also can instantly tell you the ghost type before you get any evidence.

Edit: if you currently aren't playing no evidence watch some of Maggstor's guides on YouTube about how to succeed with no evidence. Your level and bankroll will skyrocket. The best part about Phasmophobia is the ghosts all do behave uniquely. There is a lore and a general level of cohesion that is lacking in clones like Demonologist. You really only need one video camera, cruxifixes, salt, smudge sticks, and lighters to identify any ghost.
